pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: a new set of laws after the refusal to enter the land
decisions.reason: Chapter 14 ended with the people refusing to go into Canaan and being told that the adults would die in the wilderness (14:28-35). This chapter turns to laws for life in the land, and the speech formula marks the first of three speeches (verses 1, 17, 37).

records.heading: Grain and drink offerings with the sacrifices

records.source: דַּבֵּר֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם כִּ֣י תָבֹ֗אוּ אֶל־אֶ֨רֶץ֙ מוֹשְׁבֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י נֹתֵ֥ן לָכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Speak to [the] sons of Israel and say to them, when you come into [the] land of your dwellings which I [am] giving to you,
pieces: "Speak to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and tell them: 'When you enter the land where you will live, the land I am giving you,

L.2: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and say to them, 'When you come into the land of your dwellings, which I [am] giving to you,

R.2: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'You will come into the land that I am giving you as your home.

decisions.choice: when you come into the land: the promise still stands
decisions.reason: Right after the people were told that their generation would not enter the land (14:29-30), God speaks of the day when Israel will live there. The promise holds for their children (14:31), and these laws assume it.

decisions.choice: the land of your dwellings: the land where you will settle and live
decisions.reason: The noun means a place where people live or settle. The phrase looks ahead to settled life in Canaan, with fields, vineyards and homes, after the years in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: You will come into the land ...
decisions.reason: Readable makes the time clause a sentence of its own, so that the promise is clear, and verse 3 then begins with the offering.

records.source: וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֨ם אִשֶּׁ֤ה לַֽיהוָה֙ עֹלָ֣ה אוֹ־זֶ֔בַח לְפַלֵּא־נֶ֨דֶר֙ א֣וֹ בִנְדָבָ֔ה א֖וֹ בְּמֹעֲדֵיכֶ֑ם לַעֲשׂ֞וֹת רֵ֤יחַ נִיחֹ֨חַ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה מִן־הַבָּקָ֖ר א֥וֹ מִן־הַצֹּֽאן׃
records.gloss: and you make [an] offering by fire to Yahweh, [a] burnt offering or [a] sacrifice, to fulfill [a] vow or as [a] freewill offering or at your appointed feasts, to make [an] aroma of soothing to Yahweh, from the herd or from the flock,
pieces: and you present a food offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the herd or from the flock, a burnt offering or a sacrifice, whether to fulfill a vow, or as a freewill offering, or at your appointed festivals, to make a soothing aroma for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},

L.3: and you make an offering by fire to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfill a vow, or as a freewill offering, or at your appointed feasts, to make an aroma of soothing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the herd or from the flock,

R.3: Suppose you bring {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a food offering burned on the altar, an animal from your cattle or from your sheep and goats. It may be a burnt offering or another sacrifice. You may bring it to keep a promise, or as a gift you choose to give, or at one of your special festivals. Its smell pleases {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: an offering by fire: a gift burned on the altar for the LORD
decisions.reason: The word is related to the word for fire and is used of offerings burned, wholly or in part, on the altar. Leviticus 3:11 calls such an offering "food" for the LORD, a picture of a gift at his table.

decisions.choice: a burnt offering or a sacrifice: the two main kinds of animal offering
decisions.reason: The burnt offering was burned whole on the altar (Leviticus 1). The sacrifice was an offering whose meat was mostly eaten by the worshipers in a shared meal, such as the peace offering of verse 8 (Leviticus 3; 7:16).

decisions.choice: to fulfill a vow, a freewill offering, your appointed feasts: the occasions for these offerings
decisions.reason: A vow offering paid what someone had promised to God, often in return for help asked of him (Genesis 28:20-22). A freewill offering was given unprompted. The appointed feasts are the yearly festivals of Leviticus 23.

decisions.choice: an aroma of soothing: an offering God gladly accepts
decisions.reason: The smoke of the offering is pictured as a smell that calms and pleases God, so that he accepts the one who brings it (Genesis 8:21; Leviticus 1:9).

decisions.choice: food offering
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "food offering", as in Leviticus, and Readable adds "burned on the altar" to say what the word means. Literal keeps "offering by fire".

decisions.choice: your cattle ... your sheep and goats
decisions.reason: Readable names the animals: "the herd" is cattle, and "the flock" is sheep and goats.

records.source: וְהִקְרִ֛יב הַמַּקְרִ֥יב קָרְבָּנ֖וֹ לַֽיהוָ֑ה מִנְחָה֙ סֹ֣לֶת עִשָּׂר֔וֹן בָּל֕וּל בִּרְבִעִ֥ית הַהִ֖ין שָֽׁמֶן׃
records.gloss: then will present the [one] presenting his offering to Yahweh [a] grain offering, fine flour [a] tenth, mixed with [the] fourth of the hin [of] oil.
pieces: the one who brings the offering is to present to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a grain offering of {{units:about 2 quarts|a tenth of an ephah}} of fine flour mixed with {{units:about a quart|a quarter of a hin}} of oil.

L.4: then the one who presents his offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shall present a grain offering of a tenth [of an ephah] of fine flour mixed with a quarter of the hin of oil.

R.4: Then the person who brings the offering must also give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a grain offering. It is {{units:about 2 quarts|a tenth of an ephah}} of fine flour mixed with {{units:about a quart|a quarter of a hin}} of olive oil.

decisions.choice: a grain offering goes with every burnt offering and sacrifice
decisions.reason: The rule in verses 3-12 is that each animal offered is joined by a grain offering and a drink offering, more for a larger animal. Earlier laws ask for them only with some offerings (Exodus 29:40-41; Leviticus 23:13, 18); this law makes them part of every such gift once Israel lives in the land.

decisions.choice: a tenth; a quarter of the hin: about two quarts of flour and a quart of oil
decisions.reason: "A tenth" is a tenth of an ephah, a dry measure of about twenty quarts, so about two quarts of flour. The hin was a liquid measure of about a gallon, so a quarter of a hin is about a quart. Verses 4-5 give the amounts for a lamb or young goat (verse 11).

decisions.choice: fine flour: flour of the best quality
decisions.reason: The word names finely ground flour, the kind used for grain offerings and for fine food (Leviticus 2:1; Genesis 18:6).

decisions.choice: about 2 quarts; about a quart (units setting)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give modern measures, with the ancient ones as the alternative wording. Literal keeps "a tenth [of an ephah]" and "a quarter of the hin". Readable says "olive oil", the oil used for offerings (Exodus 27:20).

records.source: וְיַ֤יִן לַנֶּ֨סֶךְ֙ רְבִיעִ֣ית הַהִ֔ין תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה עַל־הָעֹלָ֖ה א֣וֹ לַזָּ֑בַח לַכֶּ֖בֶשׂ הָאֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: And wine for the drink offering, [the] fourth of the hin, you will prepare with the burnt offering or for the sacrifice, for the one lamb.
pieces: With the burnt offering or the sacrifice you are also to prepare {{units:about a quart|a quarter of a hin}} of wine for the drink offering, for each lamb.

L.5: And wine for the drink offering, a quarter of the hin, you shall prepare with the burnt offering or for the sacrifice, for each lamb.

R.5: For each lamb, also bring {{units:about a quart|a quarter of a hin}} of wine as a drink offering, to be poured out at the altar.

decisions.choice: the drink offering: wine poured out with the sacrifice
decisions.reason: The drink offering was wine poured out at the altar along with a burnt offering or other sacrifice (Exodus 29:40-41; Leviticus 23:13). Verses 5, 7 and 10 set its amount for each kind of animal.

decisions.choice: for the one lamb: for each lamb
decisions.reason: "The one" here has the sense "each": the amounts are for every animal offered, as verse 12 says. The command now addresses each worshiper as "you" (singular).

decisions.choice: to be poured out at the altar
decisions.reason: Readable adds what a drink offering is, since the term alone does not say what was done with the wine.

records.source: א֤וֹ לָאַ֨יִל֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה מִנְחָ֔ה סֹ֖לֶת שְׁנֵ֣י עֶשְׂרֹנִ֑ים בְּלוּלָ֥ה בַשֶּׁ֖מֶן שְׁלִשִׁ֥ית הַהִֽין׃
records.gloss: Or for the ram you will prepare [a] grain offering, fine flour two tenths, mixed with oil, [the] third of the hin.
pieces: For a ram, prepare a grain offering of {{units:about 4 quarts|two tenths of an ephah}} of fine flour mixed with {{units:about 1 1/4 quarts|a third of a hin}} of oil.

L.6: Or for a ram you shall prepare a grain offering of two tenths [of an ephah] of fine flour mixed with a third of the hin of oil.

R.6: If you offer a ram, bring a grain offering of {{units:about 4 quarts|two tenths of an ephah}} of fine flour mixed with {{units:about 1 1/4 quarts|a third of a hin}} of olive oil.

decisions.choice: two tenths; a third of the hin: more for a larger animal
decisions.reason: The amounts grow with the animal: for a lamb a tenth of an ephah of flour and a quarter of a hin of oil and of wine (verses 4-5), for a ram two tenths and a third (verses 6-7), for a bull three tenths and a half (verses 9-10). Two tenths of an ephah is about four quarts, and a third of a hin about one and a quarter quarts. The same scale is used for the daily and festival offerings (28:12-14).

decisions.choice: about 4 quarts; about 1 1/4 quarts (units setting)
decisions.reason: As in verse 4, Balanced and Readable give modern measures, with the ancient ones as the alternative.

R.7: Also bring {{units:about 1 1/4 quarts|a third of a hin}} of wine as a drink offering. Its smell pleases {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: an aroma of soothing: as in verse 3
decisions.reason: The offering for the ram, with its grain and wine, is a gift the LORD accepts (verse 3).

L.8: And when you prepare a young [bull] of the herd as a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfill a vow, or as peace offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},

R.8: Suppose you bring a young bull as a burnt offering, or as a sacrifice to keep a promise, or as a peace offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: a son of the herd: a young bull
decisions.reason: "Son of" with the name of a herd or kind means one young animal of it. Verse 9 repeats the phrase, and verse 11 calls the same animal an ox or bull.

decisions.choice: peace offerings: sacrifices shared in a meal
decisions.reason: The peace offering was a sacrifice of which some parts were burned, a share went to the priest, and the rest was eaten by the worshipers (Leviticus 3; 7:11-21). A vow sacrifice was one kind of it (Leviticus 7:16).

decisions.choice: a young [bull]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "bull", since the Hebrew says only "a young one of the herd".

records.source: וְהִקְרִ֤יב עַל־בֶּן־הַבָּקָר֙ מִנְחָ֔ה סֹ֖לֶת שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה עֶשְׂרֹנִ֑ים בָּל֥וּל בַּשֶּׁ֖מֶן חֲצִ֥י הַהִֽין׃

pieces: then with the young bull a grain offering is to be presented, {{units:about 6 quarts|three tenths of an ephah}} of fine flour mixed with {{units:about 2 quarts|half a hin}} of oil.

L.9: then he shall present with the young [bull] of the herd a grain offering of three tenths [of an ephah] of fine flour mixed with half of the hin of oil.

R.9: Along with the bull, bring a grain offering of {{units:about 6 quarts|three tenths of an ephah}} of fine flour mixed with {{units:about 2 quarts|half a hin}} of olive oil.

decisions.choice: he will present: the worshiper who brings the bull
decisions.reason: "He" is the one who brings the offering, as in verse 4. The command moves between "you" and "he" for the same person.

decisions.choice: three tenths; half of the hin: the amounts for a bull
decisions.reason: Three tenths of an ephah is about six quarts of flour, and half a hin about two quarts of oil (see verse 6).

decisions.choice: about 6 quarts; about 2 quarts (units setting)
decisions.reason: As in verse 4. Balanced puts the verb in the passive so that the worshiper does not change from "you" to "he" in the middle of the sentence.

records.gloss: And wine you will present for the drink offering, half of the hin, [an] offering by fire, [an] aroma of soothing to Yahweh.
pieces: And present {{units:about 2 quarts|half a hin}} of wine for the drink offering. It is a food offering, a soothing aroma to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.10: And wine you shall present for the drink offering, half of the hin, an offering by fire, an aroma of soothing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.10: Also bring {{units:about 2 quarts|half a hin}} of wine as a drink offering. It is a food offering, and its smell pleases {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: an offering by fire: the whole gift with the bull
decisions.reason: Wine was poured out, not burned, so "an offering by fire" probably sums up the bull with its grain and wine as one gift on the altar fire. It could also be meant of the wine itself, poured out at the altar where the fire burned.

records.source: כָּ֣כָה יֵעָשֶׂ֗ה לַשּׁוֹר֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ד א֖וֹ לָאַ֣יִל הָאֶחָ֑ד אֽוֹ־לַשֶּׂ֥ה בַכְּבָשִׂ֖ים א֥וֹ בָעִזִּֽים׃
records.gloss: Thus it will be done for the one ox or for the one ram or for the sheep among the lambs or among the goats.
pieces: This is what is to be done for each bull or ram, and for each lamb or young goat.

L.11: Thus it shall be done for each ox, or for each ram, or for a young one of the flock, of the lambs or of the goats.

R.11: Do this for every bull, every ram, and every lamb or young goat.

decisions.choice: ox: a bull of the herd
decisions.reason: The word names a single head of cattle. It is the same animal as "the young one of the herd" in verses 8-9.

decisions.choice: a young one of the flock, of the lambs or of the goats: a sheep or a goat
decisions.reason: The word means one animal of the flock, either sheep or goat. So the amounts for a lamb in verses 4-5 also apply to a young goat.

decisions.choice: bull
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "bull" for the ox, so that it is clearly the animal of verses 8-10. Literal keeps "ox".

records.source: כַּמִּסְפָּ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ כָּ֛כָה תַּעֲשׂ֥וּ לָאֶחָ֖ד כְּמִסְפָּרָֽם׃
records.gloss: According to the number which you prepare, thus you will do for each according to their number.
pieces: However many animals you prepare, do this for each one of them.

L.12: According to the number that you prepare, so you shall do for each one, according to their number.

R.12: Do this for each animal you bring, however many there are.

decisions.choice: according to their number: the measures are for each animal
decisions.reason: If several animals are offered at once, each one has its own grain offering and drink offering.

decisions.choice: animals
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name what is counted, the animals offered.

records.source: כָּל־הָאֶזְרָ֥ח יַעֲשֶׂה־כָּ֖כָה אֶת־אֵ֑לֶּה לְהַקְרִ֛יב אִשֵּׁ֥ה רֵֽיחַ־נִיחֹ֖חַ לַֽיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Every native will do thus these [things], in presenting [an] offering by fire, [an] aroma of soothing to Yahweh.
pieces: Everyone who is native-born is to do these things in this way when presenting a food offering, a soothing aroma to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.13: Every native shall do these [things] thus, in presenting an offering by fire, an aroma of soothing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.13: Everyone born an Israelite must do these things in this way when they bring a food offering whose smell pleases {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: native: one who is an Israelite by birth
decisions.reason: The word means one who belongs by birth, an Israelite as against an outsider who has come to live among Israel. It is set beside the outsider in verses 14-16 and 29-30 (Exodus 12:19, 48-49; Leviticus 16:29).

decisions.choice: native-born; born an Israelite
decisions.reason: Balanced says "native-born" and Readable "born an Israelite", so that "native" is not taken for the earlier peoples of Canaan.

records.source: וְכִֽי־יָגוּר֩ אִתְּכֶ֨ם גֵּ֜ר א֤וֹ אֲשֶֽׁר־בְּתֽוֹכְכֶם֙ לְדֹרֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וְעָשָׂ֛ה אִשֵּׁ֥ה רֵֽיחַ־נִיחֹ֖חַ לַיהוָ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשׂ֖וּ כֵּ֥ן יַעֲשֶֽׂה׃
records.gloss: And if will sojourn with you [a] sojourner, or who [is] in your midst to your generations, and he prepares [an] offering by fire, [an] aroma of soothing to Yahweh, just as you do, so he will do.
pieces: If an outsider is living with you, or anyone else who is among you in generations to come, and presents a food offering, a soothing aroma to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, they are to do it just as you do.

L.14: And if a sojourner sojourns with you, or whoever [is] among you throughout your generations, and he prepares an offering by fire, an aroma of soothing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, just as you do, so he shall do.

R.14: Strangers may live with you, now or in the years to come. If one of them brings a food offering whose smell pleases {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, they must do it the same way you do.

decisions.choice: a sojourner: an outsider who lives among Israel
decisions.reason: A sojourner is someone not born an Israelite who has come to live among them. Such people had no family land and depended on the protection of the law, which Israel is told to give because they were sojourners in Egypt (Exodus 22:20; Leviticus 19:33-34).

decisions.choice: or whoever is among you throughout your generations: anyone else living with Israel, now or later
decisions.reason: The second phrase may widen the first to any outsider at all, or may mean those whose families have lived among Israel for generations. Either way, the rule covers every foreigner who worships the LORD while living among his people.

decisions.choice: just as you do, so he shall do: the outsider worships on the same terms
decisions.reason: An outsider may bring offerings to the LORD, and the same rules apply to him as to the Israelite (Leviticus 17:8; 22:18).

decisions.choice: outsider; strangers
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "sojourner"; Balanced says "outsider" and Readable "strangers", as in Leviticus. Balanced and Readable say "they" for the outsider, who may be a man or a woman.

records.source: הַקָּהָ֕ל חֻקָּ֥ה אַחַ֛ת לָכֶ֖ם וְלַגֵּ֣ר הַגָּ֑ר חֻקַּ֤ת עוֹלָם֙ לְדֹרֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם כָּכֶ֛ם כַּגֵּ֥ר יִהְיֶ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: The assembly — one statute [is] for you and for the sojourner who sojourns, [a] statute of forever to your generations; as you, as the sojourner shall be before Yahweh.
pieces: For the assembly there is to be one statute for you and for the outsider who lives with you. It is a lasting statute through all your generations: before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the outsider is to be just as you are.

L.15: [As for] the assembly, one statute [shall be] for you and for the sojourner who sojourns [with you], a statute forever throughout your generations; as you [are], so the sojourner shall be before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.15: The whole community must keep the same law, both you and the strangers who live with you. This law will last for all your descendants. In {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s eyes, strangers are just like you.

decisions.choice: the assembly: stated first, as the heading of the sentence
decisions.reason: "The assembly" stands at the head of the verse without a verb, naming the body the rule is for: the people gathered as the LORD's worshiping community. The Hebrew accents join it to what follows, not to verse 14.

decisions.choice: a statute forever: a lasting rule
decisions.reason: A "statute of forever" is a law that is to stand through every generation, not a rule for the wilderness only (Exodus 12:14; Leviticus 3:17).

decisions.choice: as you, so the sojourner before the LORD: equal standing in worship
decisions.reason: Before the LORD the outsider who lives among Israel has the same place as the Israelite in the matter of these offerings. The same is said in verses 16 and 29 and in Exodus 12:49.

decisions.choice: [As for]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "As for" so that the opening noun can stand in English as it stands in the Hebrew.

records.gloss: One law and one judgment will be for you and for the sojourner who sojourns with you.
pieces: One law and one ruling are to apply to you and to the outsider who lives with you.'"

L.16: One law and one judgment shall be for you and for the sojourner who sojourns with you.'"

R.16: The same law and the same rules are for you and for the strangers who live with you.'"

decisions.choice: one law and one judgment: one set of instructions and one standard of judgment
decisions.reason: The word for "law" means instruction, here the teaching on how offerings are to be made. "Judgment" means a ruling or the standard it applies. Both are to be the same for everyone (Leviticus 24:22).

decisions.choice: the speech ends here
decisions.reason: The speech that began in verse 2 ends with this verse. The next speech begins in verse 17.

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,

L.17: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: a second speech: an offering from the first of the dough
decisions.reason: The second of three speeches in this chapter (see verse 1). This one runs to verse 31.

records.heading: A loaf from the first of the dough

records.source: דַּבֵּר֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם בְּבֹֽאֲכֶם֙ אֶל־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֛י מֵבִ֥יא אֶתְכֶ֖ם שָֽׁמָּה׃
records.gloss: Speak to [the] sons of Israel and say to them, in your coming into the land which I [am] bringing you there,
pieces: "Speak to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and tell them: 'When you come into the land where I am bringing you,

L.18: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and say to them, 'When you come into the land that I [am] bringing you to,

R.18: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'I am bringing you into a land.

decisions.choice: the land which I am bringing you to: the promise renewed
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, the law assumes that Israel will come into the land, though the generation that refused to enter will not (14:30-31).

decisions.choice: I am bringing you into a land.
decisions.reason: Readable makes the time clause a sentence of its own; verse 19 then says what to do there.

records.source: וְהָיָ֕ה בַּאֲכָלְכֶ֖ם מִלֶּ֣חֶם הָאָ֑רֶץ תָּרִ֥ימוּ תְרוּמָ֖ה לַיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: and it will be, when you eat from [the] bread of the land, you will raise up [a] contribution to Yahweh.
pieces: then, when you eat the food that the land produces, you are to set aside a contribution for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.19: then it shall be, when you eat of the bread of the land, you shall lift up a contribution to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.19: When you eat the food that grows in that land, you must set some of it apart as a gift for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: raise up a contribution: set apart a portion for the LORD
decisions.reason: The verb means to lift up or lift off, and the noun is a portion taken off a larger amount and given to the LORD. Such gifts went to the priests (18:8, 11, 19). It is not the "wave offering", which is a different word.

decisions.choice: the bread of the land: the food the land produces
decisions.reason: "Bread" often means food in general. Here it is grain food made from the harvest of the land, as verse 20 shows.

records.source: רֵאשִׁית֙ עֲרִסֹ֣תֵכֶ֔ם חַלָּ֖ה תָּרִ֣ימוּ תְרוּמָ֑ה כִּתְרוּמַ֣ת גֹּ֔רֶן כֵּ֖ן תָּרִ֥ימוּ אֹתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: [The] first of your dough, [a] loaf, you will raise up [as a] contribution; as [the] contribution of [the] threshing floor, so you will raise it up.
pieces: From the first of your dough you are to set aside a loaf as a contribution. Set it aside just as you do the contribution from the threshing floor.

L.20: [From] the first of your dough you shall lift up a loaf as a contribution; like the contribution of the threshing floor, so you shall lift it up.

R.20: Give one loaf from the first of your dough as a gift. Do this the same way you give part of the grain from the threshing floor.

decisions.choice: the first of your dough: the first part of what is prepared from the new grain
decisions.reason: The word translated "dough" is rare (Nehemiah 10:38; Ezekiel 44:30) and its sense is not certain. It may mean dough or a coarse meal of crushed grain, or less likely the trough in which dough was kneaded. "The first" may mean the first batch made from the new harvest or the first portion of each batch.

decisions.choice: a loaf: a round cake of bread
decisions.reason: The word names a round or pierced loaf or cake, as used in offerings (Leviticus 2:4; 24:5).

decisions.choice: the contribution of the threshing floor: the first of the grain harvest
decisions.reason: At the threshing floor grain was separated from the stalks. The first of it belonged to the LORD and went to the priests (18:12, 27; Deuteronomy 18:4). The first of the dough is given in the same way.

records.source: מֵרֵאשִׁית֙ עֲרִסֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם תִּתְּנ֥וּ לַיהוָ֖ה תְּרוּמָ֑ה לְדֹרֹ֖תֵיכֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: From [the] first of your dough you will give to Yahweh [a] contribution to your generations.
pieces: Throughout your generations you are to give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a contribution from the first of your dough.

L.21: From the first of your dough you shall give to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a contribution throughout your generations.

R.21: You and your descendants must always give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} this gift from the first of your dough.

decisions.choice: repeated for emphasis: a lasting duty
decisions.reason: The verse repeats verse 20 and adds "throughout your generations": the gift is to continue for all time.

records.source: וְכִ֣י תִשְׁגּ֔וּ וְלֹ֣א תַעֲשׂ֔וּ אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַמִּצְוֺ֖ת הָאֵ֑לֶּה אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And if you err and not do all these commandments which Yahweh has spoken to Moses,
pieces: Now suppose you go astray without meaning to and fail to keep all these commandments that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses,

L.22: And if you err and do not do all these commandments that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken to Moses,

R.22: Suppose you do wrong without meaning to, and you do not keep all these commands that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Moses.

decisions.choice: err: go astray by mistake
decisions.reason: The verb means to stray or go wrong without intending to. Its noun, "error", is the key word of verses 24-29 (Leviticus 4:2, 13).

decisions.choice: you: the people as a whole
decisions.reason: "You" here is plural, and verse 24 makes clear that the first case is the whole congregation; the case of one person follows in verse 27.

decisions.choice: not do all these commandments: failing to keep what was commanded
decisions.reason: Leviticus 4 deals with doing what was forbidden. This law speaks of not doing what was commanded, any of the commands given through Moses (verse 23).

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on to verse 24
decisions.reason: The "if" begun here is completed only in verse 24, where the offering is set out. Verse 23 says what "all these commandments" are.

decisions.choice: go astray without meaning to; do wrong without meaning to
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "err". Balanced and Readable add "without meaning to", which is what the word means, as in Leviticus 4:2.

records.heading: Sins committed unintentionally

records.source: אֵת֩ כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁ֑ה מִן־הַיּ֞וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה וָהָ֖לְאָה לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: all that Yahweh commanded you by [the] hand of Moses, from the day that Yahweh commanded and onward to your generations,
pieces: everything that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded you through Moses, from the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} first gave commands and on through your generations,

L.23: all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded you by the hand of Moses, from the day that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded and onward throughout your generations,

R.23: This means anything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded you through Moses, from the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} first gave commands and on for all the generations after.

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses: through Moses
decisions.reason: The phrase means by means of someone. Moses passed on the LORD's commands to the people (4:37; Leviticus 8:36).

decisions.choice: from the day the LORD commanded and onward: every command, then and later
decisions.reason: The law covers the whole of what the LORD has commanded, from the first commands to those given in later generations.

records.source: וְהָיָ֗ה אִ֣ם מֵעֵינֵ֣י הָעֵדָה֮ נֶעֶשְׂתָ֣ה לִשְׁגָגָה֒ וְעָשׂ֣וּ כָל־הָעֵדָ֡ה פַּ֣ר בֶּן־בָּקָר֩ אֶחָ֨ד לְעֹלָ֜ה לְרֵ֤יחַ נִיחֹ֨חַ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וּמִנְחָת֥וֹ וְנִסְכּ֖וֹ כַּמִּשְׁפָּ֑ט וּשְׂעִיר־עִזִּ֥ים אֶחָ֖ד לְחַטָּֽת׃
records.gloss: then it will be, if from [the] eyes of the congregation it was done in error, then will prepare all the congregation one young bull, [a] son of [the] herd, for [a] burnt offering, for [an] aroma of soothing to Yahweh, and its grain offering and its drink offering according to the judgment, and one male goat of goats for [a] sin offering.
pieces: if it was done unintentionally, without the congregation being aware of it, the whole congregation is to prepare one young bull as a burnt offering, a soothing aroma to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, together with its grain offering and its drink offering as prescribed, and one male goat as a sin offering.

L.24: then it shall be, if it was done in error, away from the eyes of the congregation, that all the congregation shall prepare one young bull of the herd as a burnt offering, as an aroma of soothing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, with its grain offering and its drink offering according to the judgment, and one male goat of the goats as a sin offering.

R.24: If the community did this by mistake, without knowing it, all the people must bring one young bull as a burnt offering. Its smell pleases {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They must also bring the grain offering and drink offering that go with it, in the way the law says, and one male goat as a sin offering.

decisions.choice: away from the eyes of the congregation: without the congregation knowing
decisions.reason: What is done "from the eyes" of someone is hidden from them. The whole people failed in something without being aware of it (Leviticus 4:13).

decisions.choice: a bull as a burnt offering and a male goat as a sin offering
decisions.reason: In Leviticus 4:14 the congregation brings a bull as a sin offering. Here it brings a bull as a burnt offering and a male goat as a sin offering, the same pair offered for the people at the festivals (28:11-15). The text does not explain the difference; this law deals with failing to keep commands, which Leviticus 4 does not.

decisions.choice: sin offering: the offering that removes the stain of sin
decisions.reason: This offering dealt with sin and its uncleanness, cleansing the sanctuary and the people so that the wrong could be forgiven (Leviticus 4:20; 16:16).

decisions.choice: according to the judgment: as the rule in verses 8-10 sets out
decisions.reason: "The judgment" here is the rule already given for the grain and drink offerings with a bull.

decisions.choice: as prescribed; in the way the law says
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "according to the judgment". Balanced and Readable say what it means, the amounts laid down earlier in the chapter.

records.source: וְכִפֶּ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֗ן עַֽל־כָּל־עֲדַ֛ת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְנִסְלַ֣ח לָהֶ֑ם כִּֽי־שְׁגָגָ֣ה הִ֔וא וְהֵם֩ הֵבִ֨יאוּ אֶת־קָרְבָּנָ֜ם אִשֶּׁ֣ה לַֽיהוָ֗ה וְחַטָּאתָ֛ם לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה עַל־שִׁגְגָתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And will make atonement the priest for all [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel, and it will be forgiven to them, for error it [was], and they have brought their offering, [an] offering by fire to Yahweh, and their sin offering before Yahweh, for their error.
pieces: The priest is to make atonement for the whole congregation of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, and they will be forgiven, because it was a mistake and they have brought their offering, a food offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and their sin offering before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for their mistake.

L.25: And the priest shall make atonement for all the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and it will be forgiven them, for it [was] an error, and they have brought their offering, an offering by fire to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and their sin offering before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for their error.

R.25: The priest will make atonement for the whole community of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, and they will be forgiven. This is because they did wrong without meaning to, and they brought {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their offerings for it: a food offering and a sin offering.

decisions.choice: make atonement: the rite that deals with sin
decisions.reason: The priest's work with the blood of the offerings removes the guilt and stain of the wrong so that the people are right with God again (Leviticus 1:4; 16:30).

decisions.choice: it will be forgiven them: God forgives
decisions.reason: The verb "forgive" in the Hebrew Bible always has God as its subject. The passive form does not name him, but the priest makes atonement and the LORD forgives (Leviticus 4:20; Numbers 14:19-20).

decisions.choice: two reasons: it was an error, and they brought their offerings
decisions.reason: Forgiveness is given because the wrong was not done on purpose and because the offerings the LORD asked for were brought.

decisions.choice: they will be forgiven
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "it will be forgiven them". Balanced and Readable make the people the subject, as in Leviticus 4:20. Readable leaves out the repeated "before the LORD" and "for their error".

records.source: וְנִסְלַ֗ח לְכָל־עֲדַת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְלַגֵּ֖ר הַגָּ֣ר בְּתוֹכָ֑ם כִּ֥י לְכָל־הָעָ֖ם בִּשְׁגָגָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And it will be forgiven to all [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel and to the sojourner who sojourns in their midst, for to all the people [it was] in error.
pieces: The whole congregation of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} will be forgiven, and so will the outsider living among them, because the whole people was caught up in the mistake.

L.26: And it will be forgiven to all the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and to the sojourner who sojourns among them, for [it happened] to all the people in error.

R.26: All the community of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} will be forgiven, and so will the strangers who live among them. The whole nation did wrong without meaning to.

decisions.choice: for to all the people in error: the whole people shared the mistake
decisions.reason: The wrong belonged to the people as a whole, so the forgiveness also reaches everyone in it, including outsiders who live among them.

decisions.choice: the sojourner too is forgiven
decisions.reason: The outsider who lives among Israel shares in the people's guilt and in its forgiveness, as verses 14-16 give him the same law in worship.

records.source: וְאִם־נֶ֥פֶשׁ אַחַ֖ת תֶּחֱטָ֣א בִשְׁגָגָ֑ה וְהִקְרִ֛יבָה עֵ֥ז בַּת־שְׁנָתָ֖הּ לְחַטָּֽאת׃
records.gloss: And if one person sins in error, then it will present [a] female goat, [a] daughter of its year, for [a] sin offering.
pieces: When a single person sins unintentionally, that person is to bring a year-old female goat for a sin offering.

L.27: And if one person sins in error, then [that person] shall present a female goat, a daughter of its year, as a sin offering.

R.27: If just one person sins without meaning to, that person must bring a female goat one year old as a sin offering.

decisions.choice: one person: the case of a single individual
decisions.reason: After the whole congregation (verses 24-26) comes one person. The word means a living being, here anyone, man or woman (Leviticus 4:27).

decisions.choice: a daughter of its year: a year old
decisions.reason: "Son" or "daughter of its year" is the Hebrew way of saying that an animal is in its first year, a year old.

decisions.choice: [that person]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb carries its subject; Literal supplies it in brackets.

records.source: וְכִפֶּ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֗ן עַל־הַנֶּ֧פֶשׁ הַשֹּׁגֶ֛גֶת בְּחֶטְאָ֥ה בִשְׁגָגָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה לְכַפֵּ֥ר עָלָ֖יו וְנִסְלַ֥ח לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And will make atonement the priest for the person who errs, in sinning in error, before Yahweh, to make atonement for him, and it will be forgiven to him.
pieces: The priest is to make atonement before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for the one who went astray and sinned unintentionally. Once atonement is made, that person will be forgiven.

L.28: And the priest shall make atonement before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for the person who errs by sinning in error, to make atonement for {{gender:them|him}}, and it will be forgiven {{gender:them|him}}.

R.28: The priest will make atonement before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for that person, and the person will be forgiven.

decisions.choice: before the LORD: at the altar in the LORD's presence
decisions.reason: The rite is done at the altar before the sanctuary, where the LORD is present among his people.

decisions.choice: it will be forgiven him: God forgives the one who erred
decisions.reason: As for the whole congregation (verse 25), forgiveness follows the atonement made by the priest.

decisions.choice: them / him; that person
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to "the person", who may be a man or a woman, so Literal uses the gender setting and Balanced says "that person".

records.source: הָֽאֶזְרָח֙ בִּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְלַגֵּ֖ר הַגָּ֣ר בְּתוֹכָ֑ם תּוֹרָ֤ה אַחַת֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֔ם לָעֹשֶׂ֖ה בִּשְׁגָגָֽה׃
records.gloss: The native among [the] sons of Israel and for the sojourner who sojourns in their midst, one law will be for you, for the one doing in error.
pieces: Whether native-born among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} or an outsider living among them, you are to have one law for anyone who does wrong unintentionally.

L.29: The native among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and the sojourner who sojourns among them: one law shall be for you, for whoever acts in error.

R.29: This same law is for everyone who does wrong without meaning to, both those born among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and the strangers who live among them.

decisions.choice: one law for the one acting in error: the rule of verses 27-28 for everyone
decisions.reason: The provision for an individual's error applies alike to Israelites and to outsiders, as the law of offerings did (verses 15-16).

records.source: וְהַנֶּ֜פֶשׁ אֲשֶֽׁר־תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה׀בְּיָ֣ד רָמָ֗ה מִן־הָֽאֶזְרָח֙ וּמִן־הַגֵּ֔ר אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה ה֣וּא מְגַדֵּ֑ף וְנִכְרְתָ֛ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִ֖וא מִקֶּ֥רֶב עַמָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: But the person who acts with [a] high hand, from the native or from the sojourner, Yahweh he [is] reviling, and will be cut off that person from [the] midst of its people.
pieces: But anyone who sins defiantly, whether native-born or outsider, insults {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and that person must be cut off from among the people.

L.30: But the person who acts with a high hand, whether of the native or of the sojourner, {{gender:that one|he}} is reviling {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and that person shall be cut off from among {{gender:their|his}} people.

R.30: But someone may sin on purpose, in open defiance. Whether they were born in Israel or are strangers, they are insulting {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. That person must be cut off from the people.

decisions.choice: with a high hand: openly and on purpose, in defiance
decisions.reason: A raised hand is a sign of strength and boldness (Exodus 14:8, of Israel leaving Egypt). Here it is set against the "error" of verses 22-29: the sin is done knowingly, in defiance of the LORD.

decisions.choice: reviling: insulting God
decisions.reason: The verb means to insult or speak contemptuously against someone, used of mocking the LORD (2 Kings 19:6, 22). A deliberate sin treats God with contempt even when no words are spoken.

decisions.choice: cut off: removed from the people
decisions.reason: The person loses their place in Israel. The law does not say here whether by death at the hands of the community or by God's own judgment; both are spoken of elsewhere (Exodus 31:14; Leviticus 20:2-6). No offering is given for such a sin.

decisions.choice: defiantly; on purpose, in open defiance
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture "with a high hand". Balanced and Readable say what it means. Pronouns for "the person" use the gender setting at Literal, since the law covers men and women.

records.source: כִּ֤י דְבַר־יְהוָה֙ בָּזָ֔ה וְאֶת־מִצְוָת֖וֹ הֵפַ֑ר הִכָּרֵ֧ת׀תִּכָּרֵ֛ת הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִ֖וא עֲוֺנָ֥ה בָֽהּ׃פ
records.gloss: For [the] word of Yahweh he has despised, and his commandment he has broken; [being] cut off, will be cut off that person; its iniquity [is] on it.
pieces: That person has scorned what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said and broken {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandment, and so must be cut off completely. The guilt rests on {{gender:them|him}}.'"

L.31: For the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} {{gender:that one|he}} has despised, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandment {{gender:that one|he}} has broken; that person shall surely be cut off; {{gender:their|his}} iniquity [is] on {{gender:them|him}}.'"

R.31: That person has treated what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said as worthless and has broken {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} command. So that person must be cut off without fail. {{gender:They are|He is}} responsible for {{gender:their|his}} own sin.'"

decisions.choice: despised: treated with contempt
decisions.reason: The verb means to look down on something as worthless. David is said to have despised the word of the LORD when he sinned with Bathsheba (2 Samuel 12:9).

decisions.choice: surely be cut off: the verb doubled for emphasis
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the verb, a way of making it certain and emphatic.

decisions.choice: its iniquity is on it: the person bears the guilt
decisions.reason: The guilt stays on the one who sinned; there is no offering that takes it away (verse 30; Leviticus 5:1).

decisions.choice: the speech ends here
decisions.reason: The speech that began in verse 18 ends with this verse. The story in verses 32-36 then shows a case of deliberate sin.

decisions.choice: their / his; them / him
decisions.reason: The pronouns refer to "that person", who may be a man or a woman, so they use the gender setting.

records.source: וַיִּהְי֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וַֽיִּמְצְא֗וּ אִ֛ישׁ מְקֹשֵׁ֥שׁ עֵצִ֖ים בְּי֥וֹם הַשַּׁבָּֽת׃
records.gloss: And were [the] sons of Israel in the wilderness, and they found [a] man gathering wood on [the] day of the Sabbath.
pieces: Once, when the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} were in the wilderness, some of them came upon a man collecting wood on the Sabbath day.

L.32: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel were in the wilderness, and they found a man gathering wood on the day of the Sabbath.

R.32: One time, while the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} were in the desert, some of them saw a man picking up wood on the Sabbath day.

decisions.choice: on the Sabbath day: the day on which all work was forbidden
decisions.reason: The Sabbath law forbade work on the seventh day on pain of death (Exodus 31:14-15; 35:2), and kindling a fire was named as forbidden (Exodus 35:3). The story follows the law on defiant sin (verses 30-31) as an example of it.

decisions.choice: gathering wood: collecting sticks or bits of wood
decisions.reason: The verb is used of gathering straw or stubble (Exodus 5:7, 12) and of a woman gathering a few sticks for a fire (1 Kings 17:10, 12).

decisions.choice: some of them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "they found". Balanced and Readable say "some of them", since not all Israel found him; verse 33 calls them "those who found him".

records.heading: A man collecting wood on the Sabbath

records.source: וַיַּקְרִ֣יבוּ אֹת֔וֹ הַמֹּצְאִ֥ים אֹת֖וֹ מְקֹשֵׁ֣שׁ עֵצִ֑ים אֶל־מֹשֶׁה֙ וְאֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֔ן וְאֶ֖ל כָּל־הָעֵדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And brought him those who found him gathering wood to Moses and to Aaron and to all the congregation.
pieces: Those who caught him collecting wood brought him to Moses and Aaron and the whole congregation.

L.33: And those who found him gathering wood brought him to Moses and to Aaron and to all the congregation.

R.33: The people who found him took him to Moses, Aaron, and the whole community.

decisions.choice: to Moses, Aaron and all the congregation: the case is brought for judgment
decisions.reason: Those who found him did not act on their own but brought him before the leaders and the people, who would carry out any sentence together (verse 35).

records.source: וַיַּנִּ֥יחוּ אֹת֖וֹ בַּמִּשְׁמָ֑ר כִּ֚י לֹ֣א פֹרַ֔שׁ מַה־יֵּעָשֶׂ֖ה לֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: And they put him in custody, for not it had been made clear what should be done to him.
pieces: They held him under guard, because it had not yet been made clear what was to be done with him.

L.34: And they placed him in custody, for it had not been declared what should be done to him.

R.34: They kept him under guard, because they did not yet know what should be done to him.

decisions.choice: custody: under guard
decisions.reason: The word means a place or act of guarding, not a prison. He was held until the LORD gave a ruling, as with the man who cursed the Name (Leviticus 24:12).

decisions.choice: what should be done to him: the matter was not yet settled
decisions.reason: The law had already said that whoever works on the Sabbath must die (Exodus 31:14-15). What had not been made clear may be whether gathering wood counted as such work, or how the death sentence was to be carried out. The text does not say.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה מ֥וֹת יוּמַ֖ת הָאִ֑ישׁ רָג֨וֹם אֹת֤וֹ בָֽאֲבָנִים֙ כָּל־הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה מִח֖וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, [being] put to death, will be put to death the man; stoning him with stones all the congregation outside of the camp.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "The man must be put to death. The whole congregation is to stone him outside the camp."

L.35: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "The man shall surely be put to death, all the congregation stoning him with stones outside the camp."

R.35: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "The man must be put to death. All the people must take him outside the camp and throw stones at him until he dies."

decisions.choice: surely be put to death; stoning him: an emphatic sentence and command
decisions.reason: The Hebrew doubles the verb "put to death" for emphasis and uses a bare verb form, "stoning", as a command.

decisions.choice: stoning outside the camp by the whole congregation
decisions.reason: The camp was holy because the LORD's tent stood in it (5:2-3), so the sentence was carried out outside. Stoning was done by the community together, so that all took part in removing the wrong from among them (Leviticus 24:14; Deuteronomy 17:7).

decisions.choice: throw stones at him until he dies
decisions.reason: Readable explains "stone" and says that the stoning is the death sentence.

records.source: וַיֹּצִ֨יאוּ אֹת֜וֹ כָּל־הָעֵדָ֗ה אֶל־מִחוּץ֙ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וַיִּרְגְּמ֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ בָּאֲבָנִ֖ים וַיָּמֹ֑ת כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־מֹשֶֽׁה׃פ
records.gloss: And brought him out all the congregation to outside of the camp, and they stoned him with stones, and he died, just as Yahweh commanded Moses.
pieces: So the whole congregation took him outside the camp and stoned him to death, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

L.36: And all the congregation brought him out to outside the camp, and they stoned him with stones, and he died, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

R.36: So all the people took him outside the camp and threw stones at him until he died. They did just what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

decisions.choice: just as the LORD commanded Moses: the verdict carried out exactly
decisions.reason: The phrase, used throughout the books of Moses for obedience to God's commands, here marks that the people did exactly what the LORD had said.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

L.37: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: a third speech: tassels as a reminder
decisions.reason: The third speech of the chapter (see verse 1), on tassels that help Israel remember the commandments, follows the story of a man who broke one of them.

records.heading: Tassels on the corners of clothing

records.source: דַּבֵּ֞ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם וְעָשׂ֨וּ לָהֶ֥ם צִיצִ֛ת עַל־כַּנְפֵ֥י בִגְדֵיהֶ֖ם לְדֹרֹתָ֑ם וְנָֽתְנ֛וּ עַל־צִיצִ֥ת הַכָּנָ֖ף פְּתִ֥יל תְּכֵֽלֶת׃
records.gloss: Speak to [the] sons of Israel and say to them, and they will make for themselves tassel[s] on [the] corners of their garments to their generations, and they will put on [the] tassel of the corner [a] cord of blue.
pieces: "Speak to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. Tell them that in every generation they are to make tassels for the corners of their clothing and fasten a blue cord to the tassel at each corner.

L.38: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and say to them [that] they shall make for themselves tassels on the corners of their garments throughout their generations, and they shall put on the tassel of each corner a cord of blue.

R.38: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} that for all time to come they must make tassels for the corners of their clothes. On the tassel at each corner they must tie a blue cord.

decisions.choice: tassels: twisted threads hanging from the garment
decisions.reason: The word means a fringe or tassel; it is also used of a lock of hair (Ezekiel 8:3). The singular is used for the tassels as a group, one at each corner.

decisions.choice: the corners of their garments: the outer cloak
decisions.reason: The everyday outer garment was a large piece of cloth with four corners, worn as a cloak and used as a blanket at night (Exodus 22:25-26; Deuteronomy 22:12).

decisions.choice: blue: a costly blue or violet dye
decisions.reason: The dye was made from sea snails and was very expensive. It colored the curtains of the tabernacle and the high priest's robe (Exodus 26:1; 28:31). A cord of it on everyone's clothes marked every Israelite as belonging to the holy God (verse 40).

decisions.choice: tell them that ... they are to make
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the command into reported speech. The direct words of the LORD to the people begin in verse 39, where the Hebrew turns to "you".

records.source: וְהָיָ֣ה לָכֶם֮ לְצִיצִת֒ וּרְאִיתֶ֣ם אֹת֗וֹ וּזְכַרְתֶּם֙ אֶת־כָּל־מִצְוֺ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם אֹתָ֑ם וְלֹֽא־תָתֻ֜רוּ אַחֲרֵ֤י לְבַבְכֶם֙ וְאַחֲרֵ֣י עֵֽינֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־אַתֶּ֥ם זֹנִ֖ים אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And it will be for you as [a] tassel, and you will see it and remember all [the] commandments of Yahweh and do them, and not you will go about after your heart and after your eyes, after which you [are] prostituting,
pieces: 'Whenever you see this tassel, it will remind you of all the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, so that you do them and do not wander after your own heart and your own eyes, following them in unfaithfulness,

L.39: 'And it shall be a tassel for you, and you shall look at it and remember all the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and do them, and you shall not go about after your heart and after your eyes, after which you prostitute yourselves,

R.39: 'When you look at the tassel, you will remember all {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s commands and obey them. You will not just follow whatever your heart wants and your eyes see. Following them is like being unfaithful in a marriage.

decisions.choice: go about: the word used of the spies
decisions.reason: The verb means to go about exploring or searching out. It is the word used for the spies who went to scout the land (13:2, 16-17; 14:34). Israel had followed what the spies saw rather than what the LORD said; the tassel is to keep them from following their own eyes.

decisions.choice: after your heart and after your eyes: your own desires and what attracts you
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought and will, and the eyes the way desire is drawn to things. To go after them is to be led by one's own wishes instead of God's commands.

decisions.choice: prostituting: unfaithfulness to God
decisions.reason: Israel's turning from the LORD is often pictured as sexual unfaithfulness (Exodus 34:15-16; Judges 2:17). The noun from the same verb is used of the people's unfaithfulness in 14:33.

decisions.choice: it shall be a tassel for you: the tassel with its blue cord
decisions.reason: "It" is the tassel the LORD has just described; seeing it is meant to bring the commands to mind. The sentence runs on into verse 40.

decisions.choice: like being unfaithful in a marriage
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture behind the word instead of reproducing it. Balanced says "in unfaithfulness"; Literal keeps "prostitute yourselves".

records.source: לְמַ֣עַן תִּזְכְּר֔וּ וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם אֶת־כָּל־מִצְוֺתָ֑י וִהְיִיתֶ֥ם קְדֹשִׁ֖ים לֵֽאלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: so that you will remember and do all my commandments, and you will be holy to your God.
pieces: so that you remember and do all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments and are holy to your God.

L.40: so that you may remember and do all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments, and be holy to your God.

R.40: So remember all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commands and obey them. Then you will be holy, set apart for your God.

decisions.choice: holy to your God: set apart for God and belonging to him
decisions.reason: To be holy is to belong to God and to share his character (Leviticus 11:44; 19:2). Here the whole people, not only the priests, are called to be holy by keeping his commands.

decisions.choice: my commandments: the LORD speaks of himself
decisions.reason: Verse 39 spoke of "the commandments of the LORD"; here the LORD calls them his own, and verse 41 names him.

decisions.choice: set apart for
decisions.reason: Readable adds "set apart for" to say what being holy to God means.

pieces: I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.'"

decisions.choice: who brought you out of Egypt to be your God: the ground of the commands
decisions.reason: The LORD's rescue of Israel from Egypt is the reason they are to obey him; he freed them so that they would belong to him as their God (Exodus 6:7; 20:2; Leviticus 11:45).

decisions.choice: I am the LORD your God, repeated: a closing seal
decisions.reason: The words open and close the verse, framing the law and the chapter with the LORD's own name.
